newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ceval to invest $26 mln in port.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ceval to invest $26 mln in port.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Ceval Alimentos SA will invest $26 million in expanding warehouse capacity and building a terminal for soybeans and soyproducts in Sao Francisco do Sul port, a spokeswoman said.
The investment in the southern port, due to be made in two stages over the next 18 months, is aimed at reducing the company's export costs.
In the first stage, Ceval will invest $7 million in building its own warehouse with a capacity of 80,000 tonnes at the terminal it is currently using.

"At the moment, we are using a CIDASC warehouse with a capacity of 200,000 tonnes and we will continue to operate from this terminal," director-general Vilmar de Oliveira Schurmann was quoted as saying by private news agency Invest News.
In the second phase, Ceval will spend $19 million on building its own terminal and a second warehouse with capacity of 120,000 tonnes, both due to be completed by the end of 1997.
The spokeswoman said that when the project was completed, Ceval would export 2.5 million tonnes of soybean and soyproducts per year, up 500,000 tonnes from the current level.
Shurmann told Invest News that Ceval's export costs would drop by approximately $3 per tonne to around $4, representing savings of $7.5 million per year.
Ceval expects turnover of $2.8 billion in 1996, of which exports are forecast to account for $1.2 billion.
